title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (Apr 2027 data), 10:00 ET — the May triple-header, and the one May slot the FOMC does not share
source: EST: ISM's own release-schedule paragraph as read verbatim onto this calendar by ism-manufacturing-2027-01-05 from the August-2026 report (PRNewswire, dateline Tempe, Ariz., 2026-09-01) — 'The full text version of the ISM(R) Manufacturing PMI(R) Report is posted on ISM(R)'s website at www.ismrob.org on the first business day* of every month after 10:00 a.m. ET. The one exception is in January when the report is released on the second business day of the month.' with the footnote '*Unless the New York Stock Exchange is closed.' May 2027 opens on Saturday 2027-05-01, so the first business day is Monday 2027-05-03; it is not a US federal holiday (the nearest is Memorial Day, already tracked as memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31) and the NYSE trades a normal session. Not January, so the second-business-day exception does not apply. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VALIDATED 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research, which rebuilt the release-day set from the trading calendar itself (Yahoo SPY daily bars, 2005-01-03 -> 2026-09-09, 5,455 sessions) and confirmed the rule reproduces 22 for 22 on May editions since 2005 and 261 for 261 across all months, the NYSE-closure footnote handled automatically by deriving the first TRADING day rather than the first calendar business day. ismworld.org was re-probed direct on 2026-09-09 and returned HTTP 400 at the end of an eleven-hop self-referential redirect chain under a browser user-agent (.../news-publications/ repeated eleven times before /reports/ism-pmi-reports/manufacturing/) — a new failure mode distinct from the 922-byte Google-reCAPTCHA page the 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-05 sibling sessions recorded, and the seventh consecutive session locked out. No 2027 ROB calendar could be read and the prefix stays EST:. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03, 2026-09-09; canonicalised from proposals/ism-manufacturing-2027-05-03.from-treasury-borrowing-estimates-2027-05-03.json by its own initial research the same day
notes: THE MAY TRIPLE-HEADER. This session carries ISM Manufacturing at 10:00 ET, SLOOS at 14:00 ET and the Treasury quarterly borrowing estimates at 15:00 ET, with the refunding statement 2027-05-05 and payrolls 2027-05-07 — a close-to-close read of 2027-05-03 contains all three. The configuration is calendar geometry, not coincidence: an FOMC decision on a Wednesday in the last week of April puts SLOOS and the borrowing estimates on the following Monday, and when May 1 falls on a Saturday or Sunday that Monday is also May's first trading day, hence ISM's. Measured over 2005-2026 it has occurred exactly FOUR times — 2010-05-03, 2011-05-02, 2016-05-02, 2021-05-03 — and 2027-05-03 is the fifth. THE ATTRIBUTION FINDING THAT MATTERS, and it corrects a naive read of the sibling chain. The May slot looks bond-bearish in aggregate (^TNX +1.455% mean on 12 May releases 2015-2026 against -0.034% on the other 129, TLT -0.520% vs +0.079%), which would tempt a supply story. Splitting the 22 May releases since 2005 by their relation to the April/May FOMC decision (decision dates parsed direct from federalreserve.gov's fomccalendars.htm and fomchistorical2005-2020.htm, all HTTP 200, 2026-09-09) dissolves it: the entire tilt sits in the EIGHT years the ISM day preceded the decision (^TNX +1.646%, up 7 of 8; TLT -0.877% against +0.071% for the other 14, permutation p=0.017; IEF -0.396% vs -0.021%, p=0.018), while the three years the decision landed ON the ISM day ran the other way (^TNX -1.337%, TLT +0.726%). 2027-05-03 is in NEITHER arm — it sits three sessions AFTER the 2027-04-28 decision and 26 sessions before 2027-06-09 — and its own four-observation bucket, the triple-header, is flat: ^TNX +0.475% against +0.970% on the other 18 Mays (p=0.631), TLT -0.229% vs -0.283% (p=0.922), SPY +0.538% (p=0.382), yields up on 2 of 4. So the slot's headline number does not belong to this date, and the honest posture is a refusal with a receipt rather than a fade. Impact HIGH matches the six existing ism-manufacturing entries and their unchanged reasoning: prices-paid and new-orders reprice the Fed-cut path and 10Y real yields, i.e. the discount rate on long-duration tech, the only channel from this corridor that reaches this calendar's AI names at all.
